Built with Android Jetpack, Kotlin, OkHttp, Retrofit, SQLCipher and Haze - all open-source software under their respective licenses.
PocketOS collects only what it needs to work. Here is exactly what happens with your information.

Reminders, tasks, subscriptions, categories, your settings and a short local history of completed reminders. The database is encrypted with a key protected by Android Keystore. Notification sounds and app-lock settings never leave the device.
Uploaded to the server (only with an account)

Your e-mail, a password hash (never the password), your display name, and the reminders, subscriptions, custom categories and synced preferences you create. Sign-in sessions record the device name and app version. Security logs store a one-way hash of your IP address, never the address itself.
Changes are saved on the device first and uploaded over HTTPS when you are online. Each device downloads only what changed. Without an account, nothing is uploaded.

Export your device or account data at any time from Settings → Export & delete. Deleting your account permanently removes it and all synced data from the server. Signing out removes account data from this device.

Notifications show reminder titles once your phone is unlocked; the lock screen only shows a generic message. Amounts appear only if you allow it. Widgets show titles but hide amounts by default; you can hide both.
Sign out, or turn off background sync, in Settings → Sync. PocketOS keeps working fully offline.
Data is encrypted in transit (HTTPS) and at rest on your device. Data on the server is protected by the server\'s security; PocketOS does not use end-to-end encryption.
This version contains no advertising SDK. If ads are added in future, personalized ads stay off unless you agree, and your reminders and subscriptions are never shared.
